title: The Golden Acorn Race
logline: The fastest hare in Whispering Woods races a patient tortoise, and a stream teaches both of them what it really means to win.
moral: Steady steps can carry you through anything, and helping a friend is the truest way to win.

scenes.narration: Nobody in Whispering Woods had ever beaten Hare. Not once. Not even close.
scenes.visual_description: Hare sprints joyfully down a sunny forest dirt path, ears streaming back, flower petals swirling in his wake.

scenes.narration: But Tortoise never hurried. She walked the same path every morning, one steady step at a time.
scenes.visual_description: Tortoise strolls calmly along the same sunny forest path, smiling at the wildflowers beside her.

scenes.narration: Good morning, slowpoke! Hare teased. Good morning, Hare, Tortoise smiled. You look excited.
scenes.visual_description: On the left Hare skids to a stop on the dirt path with a big grin; on the right Tortoise smiles warmly at him.

scenes.narration: Today was the Acorn Cup, a race to the Old Oak for a shining golden acorn.
scenes.visual_description: Hare gazes in wonder at a glowing golden acorn trophy resting on a mossy tree stump in a beam of sunlight.
scenes.camera: medium shot with slow reveal of the trophy

scenes.narration: Easy! Hare laughed, stretching his legs. Nobody can catch me!
scenes.visual_description: Hare stands tall with a proud confident grin, one leg stretched out, chin raised, in a sunny forest clearing.

scenes.narration: Tortoise was not fast. Yet she never quit, and she would not start now.
scenes.visual_description: Tortoise gazes ahead with calm determination, standing firmly on the sunny path.

scenes.narration: So the two friends stood ready on the sunny forest path, while the morning sun climbed above the trees.
scenes.visual_description: Both friends stand ready on a sunny forest dirt path, facing each other with cheerful smiles.

scenes.narration: Ready. Set. Go!
scenes.visual_description: On the left Hare crouches low and springs forward in a burst of dust; on the right Tortoise takes her first careful step.

scenes.narration: Hare shot off like an arrow, leaping over roots and bouncing through the flowers.
scenes.visual_description: Hare races ahead up the winding path while Tortoise follows steadily behind.

scenes.narration: Behind him, Tortoise stepped steadily forward, watching only the next step.
scenes.visual_description: Tortoise walks steadily between tall green ferns on a shaded forest trail, eyes focused straight ahead.

scenes.narration: At the top of the hill, Hare stopped and looked back. Tortoise was only a tiny dot, far, far away.
scenes.visual_description: Hare stands on a grassy hilltop in bright sunlight, looking back over his shoulder with a smug smile, the forest path stretching far behind him.

scenes.narration: Plenty of time, he yawned. Even the fastest runner deserves a little rest.
scenes.visual_description: Hare yawns widely and stretches beside a huge old oak tree, sleepy and relaxed in warm sunlight.

scenes.narration: And under the whispering leaves, Hare drifted into a deep, happy sleep.
scenes.visual_description: Hare naps peacefully beneath a leafy tree beside the trail.

scenes.narration: Meanwhile, Tortoise kept walking, past the bright flower meadow and over the soft green hills, never stopping.
scenes.visual_description: Tortoise climbs a flower-covered hill, keeping her eyes on the goal.

scenes.narration: The path grew steep and her legs ached. Just one more step, she whispered.
scenes.visual_description: Tortoise pauses on a steep rocky forest slope with a tired but determined expression and bright eyes.

scenes.narration: Then she reached the Rushing Stream. The only way across was a row of wobbly stepping stones.
scenes.visual_description: Tortoise stands at the edge of a sparkling forest stream where a row of mossy stepping stones leads across, looking at them with concern.

scenes.narration: Halfway across, her foot slipped! Tortoise wobbled, and cold water splashed all around her.
scenes.visual_description: Tortoise balances on a mossy stepping stone in the stream, wobbling with a startled look as water splashes around her feet.

scenes.narration: Stuck between two stones, Tortoise sighed. Maybe I am too slow, she whispered.
scenes.visual_description: Tortoise sits stuck between two stepping stones in the middle of the stream, looking sad and discouraged with her head slightly lowered.

scenes.narration: Back under the oak, Hare woke with a jump. The sun had moved across the sky! Oh no, the race!
scenes.visual_description: Hare startles awake beneath the big oak, eyes wide, long shadows and golden afternoon light across the forest floor.

scenes.narration: He dashed down the trail faster than ever, ears flying and heart pounding.
scenes.visual_description: Hare runs at full speed down the dirt trail through the forest, ears flying back, golden afternoon light filtering through the trees.

scenes.narration: Hare heard a splash. Tortoise was stuck in the stream, with the Old Oak just ahead.
scenes.visual_description: On the left Hare stands on the stream bank looking worried; on the right Tortoise sits stuck on a stepping stone in the stream; sunlit forest beyond.

scenes.narration: Hare could leap across and win. Instead, he looked at his friend and knew what mattered.
scenes.visual_description: Close-up of Hare's thoughtful, kind face as he glances down at something with a gentle caring expression, golden forest light behind him.

scenes.narration: Hold on, Tortoise! cried Hare. He pushed a big flat stone into place and held out his paw.
scenes.visual_description: On the left Hare kneels on the bank pushing a large flat stone into the stream and reaching out a paw; on the right Tortoise looks up hopefully from the stream.

scenes.narration: Step by careful step, Tortoise crossed, with Hare steadying her all the way. Together, they reached the other side.
scenes.visual_description: On the right Tortoise walks carefully across flat stones in the stream while on the left Hare walks beside her, gently steadying her.

scenes.narration: Thank you, Tortoise said. Go win! Hare shook his head. A race is better together.
scenes.visual_description: On the right Tortoise smiles gratefully on the grassy far bank while on the left Hare shakes his head with a warm smile.

scenes.narration: Side by side, they hurried up the golden path toward the Old Oak.
scenes.visual_description: Hare on the left and Tortoise on the right travel side by side up a golden sunlit path toward a huge old oak tree in the distance.

scenes.narration: And with one last big stretch, Tortoise's nose crossed the finish line first! The whole forest cheered.
scenes.visual_description: On the right Tortoise stretches her neck forward across a ribbon finish line beneath the big old oak; on the left Hare cheers beside her with joy.

scenes.narration: Hare clapped and cheered for his friend. I did not win the race, he laughed, but I think I won something better.
scenes.visual_description: Beneath the old oak tree, Hare claps joyfully while Tortoise smiles warmly beside him.

scenes.narration: Tortoise had proved that steady steps can cross any obstacle. And Hare had learned that helping a friend is the truest way to win.
scenes.visual_description: On the left Hare and on the right Tortoise walk home together along a forest path at sunset in warm golden light.
